connectors.name: CAN 3-pin screw terminal (top view, upper left)
connectors.orderNote: No printed numbers; vertical terminal, started at the top end (closest to the USB-C connector in the top view)

connectors.name: RS-485 3-pin screw terminal (top view, lower left)
connectors.orderNote: No printed numbers; vertical terminal, started at the top end (closest to the USB-C connector in the top view)

connectors.name: 2x6 expansion header (labels from bottom view)
connectors.orderNote: 2xN without printed numbers, read in the bottom view where the USB-C shell is at the top: position 1 = outer (left, board-edge) row at the USB end, then alternating inner/outer down the header

uncertain: CAN and RS-485 terminals: silkscreen 'CAN_A GND CAN_B' / 'RS_A GND RS_B' is printed left-to-right beside terminals whose screws run top-to-bottom; mapping CAN_A/RS_A to the top screw is inferred, not shown.
2x6 header: callout and silkscreen label columns are assumed to match the physical columns (left labels = outer/left row); the image does not draw leader lines to individual holes.
5~12V POWER DC 2-pin screw terminal skipped: only a small 'GND' silkscreen is visible above it and the other pin has no individual label, so it was treated as a power-only connector (rule 1).
notes: Labels for the 2x6 header come from the bottom-view callouts (IO05 etc.); silkscreen spelling IO5 added in functions. Board silkscreen for the second row first column is blurry (IO32/IO37 look-alike); the callout reads IO32 and was used. Callouts for CAN_RX/TX, RS485_RX/TX/EN/SE, CAN_SE, SD_* and WS2812 are on-board signals with no physical pin and were not transcribed. Square pad on the header (inner top in bottom view) is not treated as pin 1 (rule 9).
